title.narrative: Seeding a Nutrient Pollution Reduction Strategy for the coastal waters of Thailand

description.narrative: Address marine hypoxic zones by curbing coastal nutrient pollution from tourism, agriculture, and fishing ports and seafood processing in Thailand.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Yes. The Thailand CHO-IP child project will address eutrophication and hypoxia in the Inner Gulf of Thailand by reducing the release of excess nutrients. The improvement of the Gulf’s health will lead to reduced impacts on human health, environment and economy. The reduced nutrient levels and resulting hypoxia in Thai rivers and coastal areas will result in improved water quality, enhanced biodiversity and a strengthened resilience against climate change impacts. This will provide a heathier environment for local communities, directly benefiting public health and reducing respiratory and gastrointestinal issues as well as liver damage and neurological effects. In turn this will reduce current healthcare costs and strengthen food security. Improvement of the Gulf’s health will further support the fishing industry and attract tourism to Thailand to support sustainable livelihoods. The strengthening of nutrient monitoring and early warning systems for algae blooms under component 1 and 3 and the determination Total Maximum Daily Loads and awareness raising activities under component 1 will further support community health and resilience. The frameworks and policies developed under component 2 will indirectly reduce environment and human health impacts and promote businesses applying sustainable nutrient practices. The tangible improvements and knowledge-based practices in agriculture, tourism, and fishing port sector (including seafood process industry) resulting from component 3 will have long term livelihood impacts. Improved fertilizer use will reduce the expenses of farmers on their crops and a clean marine environment will attract more tourists and provide a healthy habitat for fish. These will sustain the income of local coastal communities from the blue economy. The initiatives supported by the established financial mechanism will not only support environmental efforts but ensure socio-economic benefits. The sustainable nutrient investment workshops with private sector and investors will further support improved practices can impact the livelihoods of local communities and women, in the agriculture, tourism, and fishing port sectors. The women entrepreneur training, pilot selection criteria and training targets will aim to direct additional funding and knowledge towards women(-owned businesses). The replication and scale up promoted in component 4, will further amplify these socio-economic impacts.
